assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and active sites is a foundational materials-chemistry achievement: structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and active-site control underpin petrochemical refining, emissions control and fine-chemical catalysis at huge industrial scale. The structure-to-function logic is exactly what electron crystallography and framework chemistry have been used to verify. As a structural chemist in this area I weigh the structural evidence heavily and flag my own field proximity.
assessment.attribution: The field is broad. Corma (multifunctional zeolite catalysts and active-site design), Davis (molecular-sieve synthesis and catalysis) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents, SSZ materials, Chevron) cover design, synthesis and application. Yu (framework discovery), Tsapatsis (nanosheet and membrane work) and earlier pioneers could be argued for; a three-person split is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, industrial deployment and structural characterization; recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the foundational zeolite concepts predates this candidate list and may be dispersed among earlier pioneers.
Whether the committee sees this as one discovery or an accumulation of incremental advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, a remarkable materials-chemistry story of a tunable crystalline family with defect tolerance and compositional engineering. The impact on solar-energy research is very large and the structure-property link is clear.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (first perovskite-sensitized cells with Kojima, 2009), Park (solid-state perovskite cell, 2012) and Snaith (meso-superstructured and planar devices) mark the decisive steps. Gratzel and Kanatzidis are strong alternatives, and Kojima is not on the list, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and reproducibility are well confirmed independently; long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unsettled, which argues that commercial maturity is incomplete even though the science is mature.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity may temper the committee's appetite.
Credit disputes among many contributors; Kojima's absence from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with ligand design giving broad, reliable scope. Originality and lasting impact are very high, although the 2010 prize for Pd cross-coupling may be seen as adjacent.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination with designed ligands, building on the earlier Kosugi tin-amide work. Two laureates give the cleanest configuration; Kosugi's precedent is real but the practical generality came from the other two.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over three decades with routine use in industry; recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: The 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd cross-coupling may reduce the committee's appetite.
Priority nuances between Kosugi, Migita-type precedent, Buchwald and Hartwig.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair into another without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminase fusions. It is a conceptual and chemical advance in programmable nucleic-acid chemistry, now in clinical trials. The impact on research and therapy is large.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work; Komor developed cytosine base editors and Gaudelli the adenine base editors, so the decisive contributions are clear. A single-laureate prize for Liu is also plausible. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) are credited but are a parallel, distinct line.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is early but independent reproduction in many labs and several first-in-human results make it reasonably mature. CRISPR was recognized in 2020, and the committee may see this as a derivative of it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether the chemistry-versus-biology boundary favors this work for the Chemistry prize.
Long-term safety and off-target effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduces a new pharmacological modality in which small molecules recruit E3 ligases to eliminate proteins. The concept is original and the clinical pipeline is large. Identification of cereblon as thalidomide's target gives a mechanistic structural link.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced and developed PROTACs, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others contributed, so allocation is contested and some of the credit lies in medicine.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and many structures of ternary complexes; clinical efficacy is emerging but not yet established with approved PROTACs.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Allocation across a large, overlapping field.
Medicine versus chemistry fit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from nano- and microcrystals with damage-free, time-resolved snapshots. It is closely related to my own interest in structure from tiny crystals, and it opened studies of photosystem II, GPCRs and reaction dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first demonstration (2011), Fromme provided the photosystem I nanocrystals, Hajdu developed the diffract-before-destroy concept. Schlichting also contributed substantially, so the three-person cut is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed at multiple XFEL facilities; the technique is mature, though routine reach is limited by facility access and 3D electron diffraction and microED now compete for some uses.
uncertainties: Competing and complementary methods such as microED and 3D ED.
Limited accessibility due to facility needs.
Difficult three-person allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Template-directed ordered mesoporous silica (M41S, SBA-15, MCM-48 and ordered mesoporous carbons) showed that liquid-crystal templating gives tunable mesopores in crystalline-like arrays, opening a vast area of porous-materials science. The structural analysis of these materials was a significant crystallographic challenge.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) made the M41S family, Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-15 and related syntheses, and Ryoo extended it to ordered mesoporous carbons and zeolite nanosheets. Credit is spread across at least six people and Mobil patent history complicates it.
assessment.maturity: The discovery dates to 1992 and has been confirmed widely, but real industrial applications remain narrower than hoped, which affects Nobel-level impact.
uncertainties: Limited commercial impact compared with zeolites.
Corporate versus academic credit for the Mobil team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable surface chemistry and conductivity and applications in energy storage, sensing and electromagnetic shielding. The family is new and structurally distinct from graphene and other 2D systems.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum published the first Ti3C2 MXene in 2011 and the three names cover the discovery and early development. The three-person configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive, but device applications are still early and long-term impact remains to be seen; recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Applications still being established.
Stability and oxidation of MXene materials.
Reproducibility of surface termination and composition.
